voice.text: How long to walk to the Moon? Starting at your own front door.
The Moon sits about thirty Earths away, lined up side by side, with nothing but dark between.
Walk at an easy pace, the kind you could chat through. Never stop, not even to sleep. You would arrive in about nine years.
But nobody walks day and night. You sleep, you eat, you stop to tie a shoe. So give yourself a working day of walking.
A working day of walking gets you there in about twenty-six years.
Slower adds years, quicker trims a few. Ten thousand steps a day, the popular goal, is only about seven and a half kilometers. So that trip takes about a hundred and forty years.
Apollo eleven's crew made the same trip in about three days. The distance never changed, only the speed.
